settings.heading: Two patches. One kit. Simple to use.
settings.text: Drug-free hydrocolloid patches that cover a surfaced spot and help absorb fluid: a thin one for the day and a cushioned one for the night.

settings.heading: Two patches. One kit.
settings.text: Both are the same soft hydrocolloid layer with a breathable film on top. What changes is how thin or how cushioned they are, so you can pick the right one for the moment.

settings.title: Thin and low-shine
settings.text: Sits close to the skin, so you can wear it to school, work or errands.

settings.title: Cushioned and steady
settings.text: A thicker patch that stays put while you sleep.
settings.point_2: Made to stay in place overnight
settings.point_3: Peel it off in the morning

settings.title: Cleanse and dry
settings.text: Wash your face gently and pat dry. Patches stick best to clean, dry skin.

settings.title: Press on
settings.text: Place the patch over the spot and press from the center out so the edges seal.

settings.title: Wear, then peel
settings.text: Leave it on for 6 to 8 hours, or until it turns white. Peel from an edge, toss it, and add a fresh one if the spot is still there.

settings.heading: Different spots, one simple routine
settings.text: Pick the size for the spot and the patch for the moment.

settings.title: A single spot
settings.text: A small patch that sits right over one surfaced spot.

settings.title: A few spots
settings.text: Use several small patches side by side, each covering its own spot.

settings.title: Back, shoulders, chest
settings.text: The larger body strip covers more area. Press it flat and keep it dry.

settings.title: On the go
settings.text: Keep a few in a bag and swap one when it has turned white or the edges lift.

settings.feature: Day and night formats in one kit

settings.question: How long do I wear a patch?
settings.answer: Leave a patch on for 6–8 hours, or until it turns white. Change it sooner if the edges lift.

settings.question: What is the difference between day and night?
settings.answer: The day patch is thinner with a low-shine finish so it can blend in during the day. The night patch is thicker and more cushioned so it stays put while you sleep. Use whichever suits the moment.

settings.question: Can I wear makeup over the day patch?
settings.answer: You can try it: press the patch flat, then dab a thin layer of your usual product around the edges. Avoid rubbing, which can lift the patch.

settings.question: Does it work on deep or cystic bumps?
settings.answer: No. These patches are made for surfaced spots, the kind with a visible head. They are not designed for deep, under-the-skin bumps. If a breakout is painful, large or keeps coming back, see a dermatologist.

settings.question: Is it okay for sensitive skin?
settings.answer: The patches are drug-free hydrocolloid with no active ingredients. Everyone's skin is different, so try one on a small area first. Stop using it if you notice irritation, and contact us.

settings.question: Is it drug-free?
settings.answer: Yes. The patches are drug-free hydrocolloid. They cover and protect a spot and absorb fluid from surfaced spots. They do not contain medicated ingredients.

settings.question: How many patches are in a box, and how long will it last?
settings.answer: The patch count is shown on each option above, along with the price per patch so you can compare. How long a kit lasts depends on how often you use patches.
